llm.summary: The skill is not malware, but it automatically shares project context with other skills/subagents and continues into later workflow phases without fresh confirmation.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is brainstorming to produce a project brief, but the artifact also requires War Room deliberation, multi-LLM pressure testing, a spec review subagent loop, and auto-invocation of project specification.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The triggers include broad terms like planning and requirements, and the workflow explicitly says not to prompt before continuing into the specification phase.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown skill files only; no executable installer or bundled script was present, and static scan plus VirusTotal telemetry were clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local writes to docs/project-brief.md and .attune/brainstorm-session.json are coherent with project planning, but they may persist sensitive brainstorming content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill directs automatic local session persistence and forwards all brainstorming context to downstream skills/subagents; no credential access, destructive action, or hidden exfiltration was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an opinionated planning workflow that writes local project documents, stores brainstorming state, and may automatically invoke War Room, review, and specification steps. Avoid using it with sensitive strategy or stakeholder details unless you are comfortable with that context being passed to downstream skills or subagents; use standalone/skip options or explicitly stop after brainstorming when you do not want continuation.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: War Room integration is disclosed and related to validating approaches, but it is mandatory by default and passes all brainstorming context onward.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Auto-continuing into project specification exceeds the advertised project-brief boundary and explicitly avoids a confirmation prompt.
[SDI-2] expected: Multi-agent review supports pressure testing, but the artifact gives broad context to another subsystem automatically.
[SDI-2] expected: The spec review loop is bounded to three iterations and quality-focused, but it still dispatches generated content to a subagent and lets the main agent edit between iterations.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad ambient triggers such as planning and requirements increase the chance of unintended activation given the automatic downstream workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Saving a project brief and session state is expected for this workflow, but the artifact lacks a clear consent step before persistence.
